2) Desired unit economics: target ~$100 per 1M tokens (confirm?)

- Suggested pilot configuration (dev/test + canary traffic split) and a MVP mutual action plan.

Subject: Re: Post-call recap + pricing/latency asks

Alex — thanks for confirming. High-level pricing/ops guidance below (sketch numbers for budgeting; will follow with formal quote).

1) Pricing sketches (ballpark)
- Hosted (shared): $/1M tokens ≈ $140 (streaming enabled) — best for fast time-to-value but higher unit cost due to multi-tenant overhead and limited reserved capacity.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): $/1M tokens ≈ $60–$110 depending on commit (higher commit → lower unit price). Predictable throughput, better p95 tail latency.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): custom — usually similar to Dedicated but with additional platform fees.

Given your budget (~$8k–$12k/month) and target $/1M ≈ $100: 100M tokens at $100/1M → $10k/month (fits within range). If you hit 200M tokens, Dedicated reserved pricing would drop unit costs materially.

2) Latency vs cost trade-offs (short)
- Streaming vs batching: streaming (smaller request chunks, immediate token flush) improves UX but reduces batching efficiency → unit cost +15–30% vs highly batched inference.
- Batching settings: increasing batch size or accepting small additional tail latency can reduce per-token compute cost significantly; e.g., batch window 20–50ms vs 200ms can change throughput and p99 by notable amounts.
- SLO-driven pricing: we can structure a pilot where certain percentage of traffic is on a latency-backed tier (lower unit cost for non-SLO traffic, higher for SLO-backed traffic).

3) Proposed pilot (2–4 weeks)
- Traffic: up to 100k calls/day (mix chat + summary).
- Config: Hosted API with a canary route on Dedicated for 10% of traffic to measure p95 improvements.
- Observability: we'll provide token-level cost breakdown and per-route latency dashboards.

I'll produce a formal quote (with committed thresholds) — can you confirm procurement contact and desired pilot start date (you mentioned early Sept?)

Best,
Marcus

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Post-call recap + pricing/latency asks — technical notes

Alex — quick technical notes to help with the quote and pilot design: 

- Streaming best practices: for chat UX we recommend streaming tokens for turn-by-turn replies. To preserve unit economics: use response chunking + prefix caching where possible.
- Caching: prefix/KV caching for repetitive system prompts can reduce token consumption by up to 20% for templated workflows (saves cost and latency).
- Batching strategy: for user-facing chat aim for a batch window of 20–50ms in Dedicated to balance latency and batching efficiency. For background summarization job queue, use larger batch windows (200–500ms) to maximize throughput.

Example unit economics (illustrative)
- Baseline: 1M tokens at Dedicated $90/1M → $90.
- If streaming premium +20% → $108/1M.
- With caching that reduces token spend by 15% effective cost per delivered token → ~ $91/1M effective.

We can run a small A/B during the pilot to measure real delta and tune batch windows. If you want, we'll include a 1-pager showing measured latency vs cost at different batch windows.

Monica
